transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… work got out of hand. I was taking on all these plant redesign projects, calling suppliers after hours, rewriting shift plans myself. Then suddenly I couldn’t keep up with the same plans I’d started. It’s been… a lot.
During that time when you were taking on all those projects and calling suppliers after hours, did you feel unusually energized or wired compared with your normal self?

Yeah… I did. I had this extra energy, like I didn’t really know what to do with it. I’d be unpacking after midnight, reorganizing things at home, answering work emails… and still thinking I should go back to the plant to check one more thing.
During that high-energy period, did you need less sleep than usual?
Yeah. I mean… I was sleeping maybe two or three hours, and I’d still show up at the plant feeling pretty sharp. Charged, almost. Like sleep was… optional, or kind of inefficient.
During that high-energy time, did you feel unusually confident or like you could handle things other people couldn’t?

Yeah… I guess I did. I thought I could fix the whole production workflow myself, faster than the consultants. When people raised concerns, I kind of brushed them off… like failing wasn’t really possible.
During that high-energy time, were you talking more than usual?
Yeah… I think so. In meetings I’d catch myself talking faster than normal, going on longer. I’d jump from line speeds to staffing to supplier problems before anyone really had a chance to answer.
During that high-energy time, did you have any experiences like hearing things other people couldn’t hear or believing things that others said weren’t true?
No… not really. I don’t think I heard things or anything like that. I had strong opinions, but… not like voices or something.
During that high-energy period, did it cause serious problems at work or at home?

Yeah… it did. Work especially. I got to the point where I had to ask to be taken out of a shift-planning meeting, because I just… couldn’t make the basic production decisions I’m supposed to make. Occupational health ended up getting involved.
About how many days did that unusually high-energy period last?
Um… about three weeks, I think. Since I moved into the temporary apartment. It’s been… on and off, but that whole intense period started around then.
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… I think so. Lately I’ve been waking up in the temporary apartment with this really heavy, kind of hollow feeling. Like the day’s already ruined before I even get in the car to go to the plant.
During this recent low period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m… not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to that, I guess. Things just feel kind of flat, but I don’t know if I’d call it losing interest.
During that high-energy period, were you hospitalized for it?
No… I don’t think so. I wasn’t in the hospital for it.
During this recent low period, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… most days. I wake up in that temporary apartment and it’s just this heavy, hollow feeling, like everything’s already ruined before I even leave for the plant.
During this recent low period, have you noticed a clear loss of interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know. I mean, things feel muted, I guess… but I haven’t really tracked whether I’m actually not enjoying them or just not paying attention.
During that high-energy period, did it get so severe that you were unable to function at work or in your usual responsibilities?

Yeah… I mean, it wasn’t just me being “productive.” I had to ask to be pulled out of a shift-planning meeting, and occupational health got involved because I wasn’t really able to make the basic production calls I’m supposed to make.
During that high-energy period, were you able to keep doing your normal work responsibilities?
Not really, no. I had to step out of a shift-planning meeting… and occupational health got pulled in. I just wasn’t able to make the basic production decisions I’m supposed to make.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview documents a clear manic episode lasting about three weeks with elevated/overactive energy, markedly decreased need for sleep, inflated confidence, increased talkativeness, and significant occupational impairment severe enough to disrupt normal job functioning. Psychotic symptoms and hospitalization were denied. The patient also reports a recent depressive period, supporting a bipolar-spectrum illness. Given the candidate set and the absence of psychotic features, the best-fitting diagnosis is bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic without psychotic symptoms.
